question: A man sells two mobile phones for Rs. 6,000 each, gaining 25% on one and losing 25% on the other. What is his gain or loss percent in whole transaction (up to two decimal places)?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] **__Shortcut Trick__**Total SP of two mobiles = 6000 + 6000 = Rs. 12,000

Total CP of two mobiles 

⇒ 6000 × (100/125) + 6000 × (100/25) = Rs. 12,800

**∴ Loss% = (800/12800) × 100 = 6.25% Loss**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__** 

**Given:**

The salesman mobile phones for Rs.6000 each

He gained 25% on one and lost 25% on second

**Formula used:**

Loss% = (Loss/C.P) × 100

Where, C.P = Cost Price & S.P = Selling Price

**Calculation:**

Let the C.P of the mobile be Rs. a and Rs. b respectively.

He gained 25% on one while lost 25% on the other.

a + 25% of a = 6000

⇒ 1.25a = 6000

⇒ a = Rs. 4800

Again, b – 25% of b = 6000

⇒ 0.75b = 6000

⇒ b = Rs. 8000

Total C.P = Rs. 4800 + 8000 = Rs. 12800

Total S.P = Rs. 6000 + 6000 = Rs. 12000 Since,

C.P > S.P

So, there will be a loss in this transaction

Loss = 12800 – 12000 = Rs. 800

Loss% = (800/12800) × 100 = 6.25% Loss

**∴ The loss percent in this transaction is 6.25%.**
